summary: Ernest B. Havell (1861–1935) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Reading School and the Royal College of Art, later serving as Superintendent at Chennai's Government College of Fine Arts and Keeper at Calcutta's Government College of Art and Craft.

Ernest Bender (1919–1996) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Henry Hoenigswald, and Zellig Harris. He served as Assistant Professor at the University of Pennsylvania and edited the JAOS.
Ernest Clerc de Landresse (1800–1862) was a scholar in Sinology and Japanology. He studied at the École des chartes and under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat.

Ernest Fenollosa (1853–1908) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and art history. Educated at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, he taught at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of the Arts, and Tokyo University of Education, and curated at MFA Boston.

Ernest Herbert Cooper Walsh (1865–1952) worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Trent College and University College London, later serving as Lecturer in Tibetan at SOAS and Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Oxford (1920–1921).

Ernest John Henry Mackay (1880–1943) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol, training under Flinders Petrie and John Marshall. He held posts in Mandatory Palestine and the Archaeological Survey of India.
Ernest Monnington Bowden (1859–1904) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was educated at Malvern College and Pembroke College, Cambridge.
Ernest Paxton Janvier (1890–1962) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his education at Princeton University (A.B.) and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D.).

Ernest Philip Horrwitz (1866–1928) was an Indologist. He held academic posts as Sanskrit Professor at Trinity College Dublin, Sanskrit Instructor at City College of New York, lecturer at the universities of Mumbai and Rangoon, and teacher at Hunter College.

Ernest Renan (1823–1892) was a French scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and history. He studied at Saint-Sulpice and the Collège de France under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère, later becoming professor of Hebrew and administrator at the Collège de France.

Ernest Sosa (born 1940) is an American philosopher. He studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as professor at Brown University and Board of Governors Professor of Philosophy at Rutgers University.

Ernst Arbman (1891–1959) worked in Indology and religious studies. He earned multiple degrees at Uppsala University, studying under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Jarl Charpentier, before teaching there and serving as Professor of Comparative Religion at Stockholm University (1937–1958).
Ernst Arthur Voretzsch (1868–1965) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen from circa 1888 to 1891.

Ernst Carl Büchi (1914–1981) worked in Indology and anthropology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Otto Schlaginhaufen and at the University of Copenhagen, later serving at the Anthropological Survey of India and as anthropology professor at Free University of Berlin.
Ernst Cassirer (1874–1945) was a philosopher educated at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg. He held posts at Berlin, Hamburg, Oxford, Gothenburg, Yale, and Columbia.

Ernst Cohn-Wiener (1882–1941) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Berlin and Heidelberg, he taught at the Humboldt-Akademie and directed the Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery.

Ernst Curtius (1814–1896) was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis, later serving as professor at Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, and director of the Altes Museum.

Ernst Fraenkel (1881–1957) was a German linguist. He studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Leipzig under Johannes Schmidt, August Leskien, and Wilhelm Schulze. He served as ordinary professor at Kiel University and later taught at the University of Hamburg.

Ernst Förstemann (1822–1906) was a scholar in linguistics and history. He studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under Karl Lachmann, Franz Bopp, and August Friedrich Pott, later heading the Saxon State and University Library Dresden.

Ernst Fürlinger (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he also lectured, and held research and leadership positions at the University for Continuing Education Krems.
